sentences.text:
This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the
petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.189/2022, registered at Police Station
Napasar, District Bikaner, for offences under Sections 498A, 406, 304B & 34 Ipc.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the allegation of the prosecution is that deceased- Gayatri on 06.11.2022, committed suicide by hanging herself at 09:30 pm, when she was in her paternal home.

Learned counsel submitted that though, there is an allegation against the petitioner of [2023:RJ-JD:30085] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-11543/2023] subjecting the deceased to mental and physical cruelty in connection with dowry demand but the present case is not a case of dowry death.

Learned counsel submitted that as a matter of fact, the deceased was not happy with her husband on certain issues and therefore, she committed suicide after having some discussion with the petitioner on mobile, soon before committing suicide.

Learned counsel submitted that no independent witness Ramkumar Tarad vs State Of Rajasthan on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108857864/
1 has levelled allegation against the petitioner regarding raising any demand or causing harassment for dowry to the deceased.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that co-accused Arjun Ram (SB CRLMB No.5196/2023) has already been enlarged on bail by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 24.08.2023.

Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 20.01.2023, challan has already been filed and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time,
therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-petitioner.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant have opposed the bail application and submitted that the deceased committed suicide due to harassment caused to her in connection with demand for dowry.

Attention of the Court was drawn towards the FIR, statement of complainant and other family members of the deceased recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.,
wherein they have alleged that the deceased was meted out with bad behaviour, in connection with dowry demand.

The transcript of a telephonic conversation between the brother of the [2023:RJ-JD:30085] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-11543/2023] deceased namely Sunil and father of the petitioner namely Arjun Ram was also shown to the Court in support of the allegations.
On these grounds, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant prayed that the petitioner may not be enlarged on bail.

The transcript of the conversation between the brother of the deceased namely Sunil and father of the petitioner namely Arjun Ram is reproduced below:-
"FkS ds Egkusa iyk Hkkjh djok fn;k gS blks FkS Egkus ds nsdj Hkqy x;k gks tks ckj &
ckj gesa vksyHkk ns jgs gks "
Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that the deceased committed suicide in her parental home; soon before committing suicide,
though the deceased and the petitioner had conversed on mobile but in case of telephonic conversation sans transcript, it is difficult to ascertain the contents of their conversation/ dispute;
co-accused Arjun Ram has already been enlarged on bail; telephonic conversation between the brother of the deceased namely Sunil and father of the petitioner namely Arjun Ram is indicative of the fact that father of Arjun Ram is merely reproaching the brother of the deceased in connection with dowry but in no way, the same can be construed as demand of dowry soon before the death;
challan has already been filed; the petitioner is in judicial custody; trial of the case is likely to consume sufficiently long time, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
[2023:RJ-JD:30085] (4 of 4) [CRLMB-11543/2023] Consequently, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Ramkumar Tarad S/o Arjun Ram Tarad arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.189/2022, registered at Police Station Napasar,
District Bikaner, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called Ramkumar Tarad vs State Of Rajasthan on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108857864/
2 upon to do so till completion of the trial.
